summary: A 1942 two-story AWS cab on a Pacific County ridge, later a state fire lookout; abandoned in 1962 when K.O. Point was built nearby, and now gone.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1962; the register says the cab is now gone.

visit.trail_note: Drive gravel road to just below the old site, then climb through the woods to the summit ridge and follow the old road. The cab is gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Willhite say the Aircraft Warning Service built the two-story cab in 1942. The 1944 AWS station report, quoted on the Washington Lookouts site, says the station used existing state-owned facilities and that the AWS added a garage. The story reports both.

sources.title: Hull Creek Lookout Site (Former Fire Lookout Sites Register)
Hull Creek Fire and AWS Lookout Site

notes_for_editor: The history agrees across sources except for who first built the 1942 cab. The register's coordinates (46.439120, -123.574570) match the record's point. The brief's second coordinate set (46.45334, -123.57404, west_us_lookouts) is not in any source read here, so the location conflict is not resolved. A WebSearch summary said the old lookout sat on the next ridge south, but the quoted newspaper text on the Washington Lookouts page says north; the page text is used. The 1956 and 1962 items are quoted secondhand from the Longview Daily News via the Washington Lookouts site. No photos added: no image URLs were available from the text fetches.
